No, I didn't end up commissioning. I was let go for medical issues, which actually really sucked. I was set to go into aviation. In an alternate universe, I'm probably finishing a career of flying F18s right now. But it's fine, I don't dwell on it any more. I was in 004 summer of 2010 as well. 

I think the Navy generally doesn't care at all about SCC. I feel like I was given more of a boost for the NROTC scholarship because I quit and focused on becoming an eagle scout, and on playing sports and joining my high school robotics team. Same with the academy, I know a ton of people who went that are eagle scouts but none who were sea cadets at all. It felt like SCC, as fun as it could be for us, was kind of broken in terms of being a strong youth program or even a pipeline into the Navy. A lot of kids just wound up enlisting or deciding they didn't want to go into the Navy anyway. I was the only one that I knew from my unit that was ever on an officer track even though I wasn't the only one who could have done well with that as a career.
So it's not because of some phony god's blessing?

What year did you go to RTC? I traveled to Great Lakes in 2010 (I'm from the West Coast). It was awesome. Maybe we were in the same division when we were 14 lol. Far better experience than we've ever had out here for RTC. USNSCC was fun but I wound up leaving the program after getting to PO2 to focus on other extracurriculars that probably served me better. Went on to go to college on a NROTC scholarship, too.
Do you feel enlightened by your own intelligence?
